classification.difficultyReason: Establish the two supplied geometric models, then apply routine forward and reverse chain-rule calculations with converted inflow units.

content.prompt: A water trough is 10 metres long, with cross section a right isosceles triangle. In this question, surface area means the exposed horizontal surface area of the water.

children.label: a
children.prompt: Show that when the water has depth $h$ cm, its volume is $V=1000h^2\text{ cm}^3$ and its surface area is $A=2000h\text{ cm}^2$.

spec.description: Open triangular-prism trough with a downward-pointing right-isosceles cross section, horizontal water surface, depth h, perpendicular marker, dashed hidden edges and longitudinal 10 m dimension. Only the mathematically relevant horizontal water surface retains shading, using house light blue.
spec.mathematics: Water depth is perpendicular to the horizontal water surface. The prism length is 10 m.
spec.answerVisibility: All diagram givens remain visible in the question edition.

answer.worked:
The right-isosceles cross section has water-surface width $2h$ cm when the depth is $h$ cm. The trough length is $1000$ cm.
$$\begin{aligned}\text{Cross-sectional area}&=\frac12\times2h\times h\\&=h^2\text{ cm}^2,\\V&=h^2\times1000\\&=1000h^2\text{ cm}^3,\\A&=2h\times1000\\&=2000h\text{ cm}^2.\end{aligned}$$

children.label: b
children.prompt: Find the rates at which depth and surface area are increasing when the depth is $60\text{ cm}$ if the trough is filling at 5 litres per minute (remember that 1 litre is $1000\text{ cm}^3$).

children.label: c
children.prompt: Find the rates at which the volume and the surface area must increase when the depth is $40\text{ cm}$, if the depth is required to increase at a constant rate of $0.1\text{ cm/min}$.

answer.short: Volume: $8000\text{ cm}^3/\text{min}=8\text{ L/min}$; surface area: $200\text{ cm}^2/\text{min}$.
